slides.title: Researchers found [[3 behaviors]] that predict losing control over p*rn.
slides.sub: Do you do any of them?

slides.title: Men [[studied]]
slides.body: A 2025 study in Addictive Behaviors of over 2,000 men looked at which p*rn habits went with losing control.

slides.title: The [[3 behaviors]]
items: Binge sessions — hours of p*rn in one sitting.
Tab-jumping — always searching for the next video.
Tolerance — needing more, or more intense, p*rn to feel the same.

slides.title: Why it [[matters]]
slides.body: These aren't just "bad nights." Researchers found them strongly linked to problematic p*rn use. They're early warning signs.

carousels.name: Sunday night reset for the p*rn-free week

slides.title: Your 30-minute Sunday reset for [[a p*rn-free week.]]
slides.sub: Step by step. Save it for every Sunday.

slides.title: [[Review]] the week
slides.body: When did p*rn urges hit? What helped? What almost broke you? Write 3 lines. That's it.

slides.title: Plan the [[danger zones]]
slides.body: Which evenings are empty? Which nights are late? Put a plan in each one before p*rn does.

slides.title: Check your [[guardrails]]
slides.body: Blocker on every device? Phone charger out of the bedroom? Accountability person updated?

slides.title: Set [[one goal]]
slides.body: Not "don't watch p*rn." Something to build: a workout, a skill, a call. Give the week a direction.
slides.note: Save this and do it every Sunday night 🔖

carousels.name: Stop treating p*rn like a reward

slides.title: You "reward" yourself with p*rn. [[That's like rewarding a diet with a binge.]]
slides.sub: P*rn isn't a prize. It's the thing you're trying to escape.

slides.title: "I [[earned]] it"
slides.body: Good week? Hard week? Finished a task? Your brain says p*rn is the prize. That's the habit talking, not you.

slides.title: It [[undoes]] the win
slides.body: You worked hard all week — then end it with guilt and a reset streak. The "reward" erases the very thing you earned.

slides.title: Pick [[real]] rewards
slides.body: A great meal. A day out. Something you've wanted. Time with people. Rewards should leave you better — not worse.
